title: OpenWeights onboarding: safety signature and runtime mapping
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an end-to-end admission workflow that attaches a verifiable safety signature, generates runtime compatibility mappings (quantization/variant candidates), and publishes a canonical pin and performance profile. This ticket covers the orchestration glue: provenance checks, deterministic transform ledger, safety/gating checks, mapping to supported runtime variants (FP16/INT8/quantized formats), and a publish step that emits artifacts to the catalog and telemetry to Console. Goal: make new community weights deployable by default into staging with a clear rollback path.
acceptance_criteria: Weights intake step verifies manifest signature and mandatory provenance fields; intake rejects if critical metadata missing
Automated conversion produces at least one runtime-compatible variant for each target backend (CUDA-FP16, Triton-INT8 sim, CPU-INT8 quantized) or records compatibility blockers
Safety signature appended using agreed token-format and stored in artifact metadata; verification endpoint returns verifiable=true for signed models
Performance profile publish job writes latency/throughput envelopes and token-cost estimates to the model catalog
Pin generation emits canonical pin and stores mapping between pin, weight SHA, and published variants
Staging smoke deploy succeeds for a sample of 10 diverse prompts and passes fidelity thresholds (per-profile checks)
technical_notes: Intake will call existing artifact-gateway API; add 3 new checks: provenance_fields, license_compat, signed_manifest_validation
Conversion is implemented as a chain: base->float32 normalization -> device-targeted quantization -> runtime-compatibility probe (unit smoke)
Use deterministic seed and dockerized conversion containers to ensure reproducible artifacts; store container image digest in provenance
Runtime mapping outputs a small JSON map: {runtime_tag: variant_pin, estimated_tokens_per_sec, memory_gb}
Safety signature uses internal signing service (kmssign.redwood) and produces a compact signature tag attached as model.metadata.safety_signature
Telemetry emitted: intake.latency_ms, conversion.failures, compatibility.status per runtime, smoke.fidelity.score; Console should surface these per-model
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed for deterministic conversion container; validated that float16 path reproduces baseline logits within tolerance on 3 small models
2026-03-05: Prototype safety signing format agreed with Security (compact JWS-like blob). Mateo demoed verification endpoint to PM and Research.
2026-03-09: Integration with artifact-gateway attempted; found missing license field in ~12% of recent community uploads — added soft-fail and metadata reconciliation task
2026-03-12: Implemented runtime probe that starts a tiny smoke server and runs 10 warmup prompts; currently fails on Triton-INT8 for models with >16k kv size — triage opened
2026-03-14: Canary pipeline wired to staging catalog; first signed pin published for test-model-alpha with initial performance profile (latency envelope and cost estimate)
review_feedback: PM (Jordan Kim): want explicit UX hooks in Console showing safety signature and exact provenance fields consumed
Design (Rina Cho): suggest a compact status badge (green/yellow/red) for runtime compatibility on model pages
Security (Priya Nair): signature format ok, but need stored audit trail for signer events (who signed, when, container digest)
Research (Evan Holt): add additional fidelity checks for long-form completion regression, not just short prompt BLEU-like scores
Infra (Samir Beg): recommend throttled parallel conversions to avoid saturating shared GPU pools; add backpressure signals
test_plan: Unit: manifest validator tests for all required provenance fields and license permutations
Conversion: deterministic re-run test (digest must match) for 5 sample weights
Compatibility: runtime probe smoke test across CUDA-FP16, Triton-INT8 simulation, and CPU-INT8 quantized runner
Fidelity: run the evaluation harness against baseline model for 100 held-out prompts; require mean token-level divergence < 0.03
Security: signature verification negative tests (tampered metadata should fail)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging only): wire pipeline to catalog with flag 'auto_publish=false' to observe outputs for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (canary): enable auto_publish for subset of trusted community repos; monitor telemetry for 48h
Phase 3 (gradual): roll out auto_publish for all community weights with rate limit and conversion concurrency cap
Rollback: unpublish pin and mark variants as deprecated; alert owners and open a follow-up for manual triage
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: conversion jobs could exhaust shared GPU quota -> Mitigation: add queued job pool with priority and circuit-breaker to fallback to CPU path
Risk: safety signature could be forged if signer compromised -> Mitigation: rotate signing keys, record signer identity and container digest in audit log
Risk: published performance profile is inaccurate for real production workloads -> Mitigation: attach uncertainty band and require periodic real-traffic validation sampling
Risk: incompatible quantized variants produce silent quality regression -> Mitigation: require fidelity gate and block publish if delta above threshold
